Ṛbhus
(‘those who shine brilliantly’)
------------------------------------------
The ऋभुस् are a class of gods often mentioned in the Ṛgveda (1.20; 1.161.6; 4.33.3; 4.34.1). Originally they were human beings, raised later on to devatva or godhood because of their extraordinarily good deeds.
Sudhanvā was a ṛṣi (sage) born in the lineage of the great ṛṣi Aṅgirā. He had three sons: Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja. (All the three came to be known as ऋभुस्.) By performing good deeds and helping the gods in हेअवेन् they became dear to these gods. Being disciples of त्वष्टा (the divine carpenter or technician) they too had become experts in the technical field. It was they who built a chariot for इन्द्र and a चमस (vessel for drinking the सोम juice) for अग्नि. They also created by their mental powers two excellent horses for इन्द्र’s chariot. They successfully restored youth to their own parents. By following the path of truth, they shone brilliantly and were endowed with tremendous powers to achieve whatever they wanted. That is why they were raised to the level of gods and were given a share in the offerings by प्रजापति himself.
They receive the सोम juice during the tṛtīyasavana (third pressing done in the evening) in the Somayāgas.
